# nanodRop

nanodRop reads the UV-Vis spectral exports from a **NanoDrop One**
spectrophotometer into R.

The instrument’s `.tsv` export stacks every measurement in one file.
Each block has the sample name, a timestamp and some calibration lines
before the actual wavelength/absorbance pairs, so it can’t be read
directly with [`read.delim()`](https://rdrr.io/r/utils/read.table.html).
[`read_nanodrop()`](https://beabock.github.io/nanodRop/reference/read_nanodrop.md)
turns the file into a long table with one row per measurement and
wavelength, ready for dplyr or ggplot2.

## Installation

``` r
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("beabock/nanodRop")
```

## Usage

``` r
library(nanodRop)

spectra <- read_nanodrop("UV-Vis 5_14_2024.tsv")
head(spectra, 3)
#>     samps waves    abs measurement         timestamp
#>    <char> <num>  <num>       <int>            <char>
#> 1:    6 1 190.0 10.666           1 5/14/2024 5:04 PM
#> 2:    6 1 190.5 10.782           1 5/14/2024 5:04 PM
#> 3:    6 1 191.0 10.853           1 5/14/2024 5:04 PM
```

Each measurement block in the file gets its own `measurement` number, so
measuring a sample twice under the same name gives two separate spectra.

Read a whole folder of exports at once. This adds a `file` column:

``` r
spectra <- read_nanodrop_dir("nanodrop_exports/")
```

Compare absorbance at wavelength pairs, as differences or ratios:

``` r
parse_waves(spectra, wave_pairs = list(c(260, 280)), type = "ratio")
#> # A tibble: 24 × 5
#>   samps measurement abs_260 abs_280 ratio_260_280
#>   <chr>       <int>   <dbl>   <dbl>         <dbl>
#> 1 6 1             1    3.39    3.13          1.08
#> 2 6 2             2    3.49    3.24          1.08
#> 3 7 1             3    2.54    2.37          1.08
#> # ...
```

![Absorbance spectra of the 24 measurements in the bundled example
export](reference/figures/example-spectra.png)

Absorbance spectra of the 24 measurements in the bundled example export

## Functions

| Function                                                                                   | What it does                                                                                                                            |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`read_nanodrop()`](https://beabock.github.io/nanodRop/reference/read_nanodrop.md)         | Read one export. Optional wavelength bounds, and optional handling of re-measured samples marked by a name suffix (`remeasure_suffix`). |
| [`read_nanodrop_dir()`](https://beabock.github.io/nanodRop/reference/read_nanodrop_dir.md) | Read every export in a folder and stack them.                                                                                           |
| [`parse_waves()`](https://beabock.github.io/nanodRop/reference/parse_waves.md)             | Absorbance at chosen wavelengths per measurement, plus pairwise differences or ratios.                                                  |

The package includes an example export
(`system.file("extdata", "nanodrop_example.tsv", package = "nanodRop")`)
and two example datasets, `ds` and `ds1`.

## Scope

This package reads the **UV-Vis spectral** export from the NanoDrop One.
It has not been tested with other NanoDrop models or with the nucleic
acid and protein report exports. If you have one of those files and it
doesn’t parse, please [open an
issue](https://github.com/beabock/nanodRop/issues) with a sample file.

## Citation

``` r
citation("nanodRop")
```

# Package index

## Reading exports

- [`read_nanodrop()`](https://beabock.github.io/nanodRop/reference/read_nanodrop.md)
  : Read a NanoDrop One spectral export
- [`read_nanodrop_dir()`](https://beabock.github.io/nanodRop/reference/read_nanodrop_dir.md)
  : Read every NanoDrop export in a folder

## Analysis

- [`parse_waves()`](https://beabock.github.io/nanodRop/reference/parse_waves.md)
  : Compare absorbance at pairs of wavelengths

## Example data

- [`ds`](https://beabock.github.io/nanodRop/reference/ds.md) : Example
  NanoDrop spectra
- [`ds1`](https://beabock.github.io/nanodRop/reference/ds1.md) : Second
  example set of NanoDrop spectra
